Figure 2:Overview of MPEG-Diffusion.The firstkkofTTsteps run at LR. At stepkk,

mixed-resolution decoder (part 3) merges the HR and LR latents into one HR video. Flames mark trained parts.

Figure 3:The VAE decoder depends on neighboring latent patches.(a) Resize-and-paste causes a seam along the resolution boundary (dashed; red arrow), even for latents encoded from a real video. (b) Noise fill spreads the error further.

Figure 4:The DiT knows where the subject is.A linear head on the DiT features at an early denoising step predicts the HR region (bright), which tracks the subject from frame00to8080while the background stays at LR (dimmed).

Figure 5:Mixed-resolution decoder.We merge the HR and LR latents before decoding. First, the LR latent
is filled with the downscaled HR region (𝒟\mathcal{D}) and upscaled (𝒰\mathcal{U}), so patches near the boundary
see less distorted neighbors. Then the mixer (GG), guided by the mask, merges the LR and HR latents into one latent
for the VAE.

Figure 7:Self-selected HR region.Top:an LLM identifies the main subject from the prompt, and Grounded SAM tracks it to produce subject masks.Bottom:a linear head on the frozen DiT features at stepkklearns to predict the HR maskMM.

other ghosted (arrows). Ours shows no visible degradation and is close to HR (more examples inAppendixA).
